english.title: Aggravated vehicle taking - ( initial taker ) death caused by accident
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), without the consent of the owner or other lawful authority, took a mechanically propelled vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), for the use of yourself or another and after the vehicle was unlawfully taken and before it was recovered, owing to the driving of the vehicle, an accident occurred by which the

(A)_[death of **(..SPECIFY THE DECEASED PERSON..) was caused]_
(B)_[deaths of **(..SPECIFY THE DECEASED PERSONS..) were caused]_

(C)_[There were no other aggravating factors]_
(D)_[There were additional aggravating factors as follows, **(..SPECIFY THE FACTORS..)]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 12A of the Theft Act 1968.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Mandatory drug test required if 18 or over
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) This wording is for use ONLY were the defendant was the 'INITIAL TAKER' - for a 'subsequent driver' see H6005 and 'being carried on' see H6006.
(ii) More than one deceased person may be named.
(iii) The penalty on indictment for this offence was raised by section 285(1) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 from ten to fourteen years with effect from 27/02/04.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Fourteen years imprisonment.

Obligatory disqualification and endorsement.

Obligatory endorsement. Licence endorsed three to eleven penalty points - only if special reasons apply.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
